newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy minister rules out future tax amnesties.
newsitem.headline: Italy minister rules out future tax amnesties.

text.p: The age of tax amnesties in Italy is over, Foreign Trade minister Augusto Fantozzi said.
"I believe that the era of amnesties is definitely passed. I don't think they would bring in any more revenue," he told reporters while attending a conference on taxation.

The finance ministry said earlier this year that a tax amnesty which closed in December last year raised over six trillion lire. Fantozzi had been finance minister in the government of Prime Minister Lamberto Dini which had introduced the amnesty.

The amnesty, under which self-employed business executives and professionals had until December 15, 1995 to file returns for back taxes, was originally earmarked to raise 11.5 trillion lire under the terms of the 1995 budget. But the government later lowered the target to some seven trillion lire.
